Rachel — thanks for the detailed list. Attaching some initial notes (redwood_forwarder_design_notes.odt) and a rough VPC sketch (vpc_network_diagram.png). Below are concrete answers and a proposed minimal architecture to review in the workshop.

Short answers up-front:
- Supported ingestion: We support syslog over TLS, Splunk HEC (HTTPS with token or mutual TLS), and a lightweight Kafka forwarder for customers who prefer push to an internal queue. HEC + mTLS is the recommended path for Splunk because it gives mutual auth and per-connector cert rotation.
- Air-gapped behavior: The forwarder runs as a sidecar or dedicated collector in the customer's subnet. It provides bounded disk buffering (configurable: 1GB default, 10GB max) and backpressure on local RT queues. When outbound is blocked, it will escalate to local persistent queue and then drop oldest logs after configurable retention thresholds — we document these SLOs in the acceptance checklist.
- Trace correlation: We propagate a Redwood-Trace ID (rwd.trace_id) in both log events (structured JSON field) and as an OTLP span attribute. We also support adding your correlation headers (x-request-id, traceparent) into exported events. Our tracer hooks will attach span ids to generation events so they can be mapped back to application traces in your APM.
- Audit delivery: We provide confirmable delivery for audit streams using HEC acknowledgements and an internal delivery ledger for 90 days (configurable). For long-term legal retention we recommend shipping audit logs to the customer's archive (S3 compatible endpoint) where you control TTL.

Proposed minimal architecture (for the workshop):
- Collector pattern: 1-2 dedicated forwarder VMs in the private-subnet (HA pair). Each forwarder runs: syslog-ng -> transformer -> Redwood forwarder -> outbound HEC/TCP.
- Network: Outbound to your SIEM via a controlled NAT/proxy or direct peering with mTLS. Firewall rules: allow egress to SIEM HEC IPs on 443 and permit internal comms on 1514 (syslog).
- Auth: mTLS for HEC + optional token fallback for ephemeral connectors. Certificates can be issued by your internal PKI; Redwood supports mutual TLS with cert rotation hooks (we'll supply API endpoints to rotate certs during maintenance windows).
- Tracing: Enable OTLP exporter on the forwarder; set sampling policy to 'always' for generation events used in audits (can be throttled).

Workshop agenda (Fri 18th, 10–12 PT):
1) Review requirements + acceptance criteria (10m)
2) Walk the minimal architecture and network ACLs (30m)
3) Sample log/trace payloads + field mappings (30m)
4) Failure modes, buffering and recovery test plan (20m)
5) Next steps & Owners (15m)

Proposed owners:

- Forwarder integration lead: Diego Fernandez (diego_fernandez@redwood.ai)
- Documentation / evidence packaging: Marissa Cole (marissa_cole@redwood.ai)

I'll be on the workshop; Kim's copied to validate the network details. If this looks good we'll lock the invite.

Diego / Marissa — a few operational clarifications before the call so we can propose concrete firewall rules and NAT/peering patterns:

1) NAT vs. VPC peering: If Acme allows egress via a fixed NAT IP range we can simply whitelist on the SIEM side. If they require no internet egress, we should validate peering or private circuit options. Peering reduces complexity but requires network change windows on their side.

2) Ports: we'll standardize on 443 (HEC), 1514/tcp (syslog-over-TLS), and 4317 (OTLP). Recommend adding a health/probe port (8081) for the forwarder so Acme's monitoring can query status.

3) Buffering policy: default disk queue = 2GB for production, max retention 72 hours of burst data at median ingest. We'll propose an acceptance test for full-disk rollover and recovery time (steps in the drive notes).

4) Evidence packaging: Marissa, can you prepare a sample evidence bundle format (logs + traces + chain-of-custody.md) that matches their SOC request? We should include checksum manifests and signed metadata.

I'll include the suggested iptables/nft rules snippet in a follow-up email and a draft firewall rule set for the workshop pack.

— Kim
Staff Reliability Engineer, Forwarder Platform
Redwood Inference
